subject: Commercial request: retention + tracing + dashboard packaging
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@aurelia.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aurelia.com
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability bundle — retention/tracing/dashboard pricing for exec review

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the low latency on streaming and the tracing drilldowns. Execs have asked for a concise commercial we can review this week. Key asks from our side:
- Retention: monthly hot retention for 90 days, with archival for 2 years.
- Tracing: ~12k active spans/day, need sampling flexibility and per-transaction cost predictability.
- Dashboards: 8 editors + ~25 viewers, need RBAC and export.

Can you send a single PDF or spreadsheet that shows: list pricing, a bundled discount path for a 12-month commit, and any pilot concessions that get us to production in 30 days? Also share any relevant SLA or audit notes we should give our security/compliance team.

Jordan Lee
CTO, Aurelia Systems
[jordan.lee@aurelia.com]

P.S. Procurement would like to see a ballpark MRR number before our Friday call.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability bundle — retention/tracing/dashboard pricing for exec review

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks.

High-level we can offer a consolidated commercial that I will send as a spreadsheet (attached: aurelia_proposal_v1.xlsx). That file will include: base list rates for retention, tracing, and advanced dashboards; three packaging tiers (Pilot, Production, Enterprise); and a starter concession model for a 12-month commit.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Ben and Soojin will map margins and confirm target discount ranges.
2) We’ll provide a 1-page SLA summary suitable for your security team.
3) Schedule a 30-minute alignment call with procurement to walk the numbers.

Can you confirm whether the tracing volume estimate (12k active spans/day) assumes 10x peak spikiness for concurrency planning? If yes, we’ll size the retention tier differently.

Thanks — sending the spreadsheet now.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai]

Attachments: aurelia_proposal_v1.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Aurelia — draft concessions and packaging idea

Hannah / Soojin — quick internal note after reviewing Jordan’s usage notes and our list pricing. My read: we have room to present a compelling bundle without going too deep on margin. Proposed structure (high level):

- Pilot tier (1–2 months): waived platform fee, reduced ingestion credits (25% off) to get them into prod quickly.
- Production tier (12-month commit):
  - Retention: priced as hot-90 + archived at 30% list; propose moving them to the "Banded Retention" SKU with a baseline at $X/mo for 90 days and archival at $Y/TB.
  - Tracing: move from pure per-span bill to a blended model — base seat + overage at per-million spans. For 12k active/day, the blended price maps to ~Z/mo.
  - Dashboards: license 8 editors + 25 viewers; offer a seat discount when combined with retention tiers.
- Commercial concession: 20% bundle buydown if they commit to 12 months and sign by EOM; otherwise fallback to standard 12% bundle discount.

Risks: netting 20% eats into our pilot credits but keeps the long-term ARR. If procurement pushes on price, we can shift to a credit-based concession (X credits applied to first 90 days) rather than upfront discount.

I’ve attached a markup with numbers (pricing_markup.xlsx) with redlines — please review and confirm whether we should go full 20% or present a two-option path to Aurelia (20% vs 12% + credits).

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[ben.carter@redwood.ai]

Attachments: pricing_markup.xlsx (XLSX)

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Aurelia — draft concessions and packaging idea

Agree with Ben’s structure; small tweaks from pricing:
- Offer path A: 20% off bundle for 12-month commit if they sign by EOM (keeps it simple for procurement).
- Offer path B: 12% off + $30k in ingestion/retention credits applied across first 6 months. Credits preserve realized revenue while lowering cash impact.
- Pilot: provide 60 days free of the dashboard editors (up to 8 editors) but cap tracing ingestion at the stated estimate to avoid open-ended exposure.

Also recommend we include a line-item for observability support hours for onboarding (priced, but discounted 50% for the pilot). That reduces time-to-value and gives CS a funded runway.

If we proceed, I’ll update the spreadsheet with two clear option rows and a short executive summary for Jordan’s exec packet.

— Soojin
Director of Pricing, Redwood Inference
[soojin.lee@redwood.ai]

Attachments: none

Subject: Proposal and options — retention, tracing, dashboards (Aurelia Systems)

Jordan — attaching a concise commercial and SOW for your exec/procurement packet. Summary below; attached: Aurelia_SOW_v2.pdf and pricing_matrix.xlsx.

Executive summary (two-option approach):

Option A — Accelerated 12-month Commit (best TCO):
- 20% off bundled list across retention + tracing + dashboards when signed by Oct 31, 2025.
- Pilot: 60 days free dashboard editors (up to 8), onboarding support (50% discounted up to 40 hours).
- Retention: hot 90 days + archival at the quoted archived rate; includes prefix caching optimizations.
- Tracing: blended model (base seat + per-M span overage). Expected bill for stated volumes: ~$Z/month (see matrix).

Option B — Moderate discount + credits (more procurement-friendly):
- 12% off bundle + $30k ingestion/retention credits applied over first 6 months.
- Pilot: same 60-day editors-free window, no onboarding discount.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached spreadsheet for line-item math (pricing_matrix.xlsx).
2) If either option looks good, we’ll schedule a 30-minute call with procurement to finalize SOW items and SLAs.

On compliance: I’m attaching a short SLA summary in the SOW PDF; our security team is available for a quick 45-minute call to walk audit evidence (SOC 2 + retention controls).

Please let me know which option your execs prefer and availability for a call later this week.

Best — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
